_meta.keyKnowledge: We are learning to investigate relationships between variables shown in graphs based on real-world data.

toLevel2.question: A graph shows the relationship between two variables using a pair of axes.
toLevel2.correctExplanation: A standard graph uses a horizontal x-axis and a vertical y-axis to display how two variables relate.

distractors.explanation: A student choosing False may confuse graphs with tables or diagrams that do not use axes.

toLevel2.question: On a distance-time graph, the vertical axis always shows time.
toLevel2.correctExplanation: By convention, time is on the horizontal axis and distance is on the vertical axis.

distractors.explanation: A student choosing True may swap the standard axis placements.

toLevel2.question: A straight line on a graph represents a constant rate of change.
toLevel2.correctExplanation: A straight line has the same gradient throughout, meaning the rate of change does not vary.

distractors.explanation: A student choosing False may confuse straight lines with changing rates seen in curves.

toLevel2.question: A steep line on a distance-time graph means the object is moving slowly.
toLevel2.correctExplanation: A steeper line means greater distance per unit of time, indicating faster speed.

distractors.explanation: A student choosing True reverses the meaning of steepness on distance-time graphs.

toLevel2.question: The horizontal axis of a graph is also called the x-axis.
toLevel2.correctExplanation: By convention the horizontal axis is the x-axis and the vertical axis is the y-axis.

distractors.explanation: A student choosing False may swap the names of the two axes.

toLevel2.question: A flat horizontal line on a distance-time graph means the object is speeding up.
toLevel2.correctExplanation: A horizontal line on a distance-time graph means distance is not changing, so the object is stationary.

distractors.explanation: A student choosing True confuses a flat line with acceleration.

toLevel2.question: A curved line on a graph always means the relationship is decreasing.
toLevel2.correctExplanation: A curve can show an increasing, decreasing or other non-linear pattern; curvature alone does not determine direction.

distractors.explanation: A student choosing True assumes all curves slope downward.

toLevel2.question: A conversion graph can be used to change between two units of measurement.
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Conversion graphs display the relationship between two units so values can be read across.

distractors.explanation: A student choosing False may not recognise conversion graphs as a practical tool.

toLevel2.question: The point where a graph crosses the vertical axis is called the x-intercept.
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Crossing the vertical (y) axis is the y-intercept; the x-intercept is where the graph crosses the horizontal axis.

distractors.explanation: A student choosing True confuses the names of the two intercepts.

toLevel2.question: On a graph showing water filling a tank, a steeper line means a slower flow rate.
toLevel2.correctExplanation: A steeper line means more volume per unit time, which is a faster flow rate.

distractors.explanation: A student choosing True reverses the meaning of steepness on a volume-time graph.

toLevel2.question: An intersection point on a graph is where two lines meet at the same values.
toLevel2.correctExplanation: At an intersection, both lines share the same x-value and y-value.

distractors.explanation: A student choosing False may not understand that crossing means shared coordinates.

toLevel2.question: A non-linear relationship always appears as a straight line on a graph.
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Non-linear relationships appear as curves, not straight lines.

distractors.explanation: A student choosing True confuses linear and non-linear graph shapes.

toLevel2.question: On a distance-time graph, what does the steepness of the line represent?
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Steepness (gradient) equals distance divided by time, which is speed.

distractors.explanation: Total distance is the y-value, not the steepness.

distractors.answer: The time taken for the journey
distractors.explanation: Time is shown on the horizontal axis, not by steepness.

toLevel2.question: A graph shows a straight line passing through the origin. What does this indicate?
toLevel2.correct: The variables increase at a constant rate from zero
toLevel2.correctExplanation: A straight line through the origin means y = mx, a proportional relationship.

distractors.answer: The variables are unrelated to each other
distractors.explanation: A clear line pattern shows the variables are related.

distractors.answer: The relationship between the variables is non-linear
distractors.explanation: A straight line indicates a linear relationship.

toLevel2.question: On a water-filling graph with time on the x-axis and volume on the y-axis, what does a horizontal section mean?
toLevel2.correct: No water is flowing into the tank
toLevel2.correctExplanation: A horizontal line means volume is not changing, so the flow has stopped.

distractors.answer: Water is flowing in at a constant rate
distractors.explanation: Constant flow would show a sloped line, not a horizontal one.

distractors.answer: The tank is being emptied gradually
distractors.explanation: Emptying would show a downward-sloping line, not horizontal.

toLevel2.question: What does the y-intercept of a graph represent?
toLevel2.correct: The starting value when x equals zero
toLevel2.correctExplanation: The y-intercept is the point where the graph meets the vertical axis, at x = 0.

distractors.answer: The rate of change of the line
distractors.explanation: The rate of change is shown by the gradient, not the intercept.

distractors.answer: The point where the line is steepest
distractors.explanation: Steepness relates to gradient, not the y-intercept.

toLevel2.question: Which type of line on a graph shows a non-linear relationship?
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Non-linear relationships produce curves rather than straight lines.

distractors.answer: A straight line through the origin
distractors.explanation: A straight line through the origin is linear.
A horizontal line is linear with zero gradient.

toLevel2.question: A conversion graph converts Australian dollars to euros. To find the euro value for $40, what is read from the graph?
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Locate 40 on the x-axis, then read across to the line and down to the y-axis.

distractors.answer: The gradient of the line at the $40 mark
distractors.explanation: The gradient gives the conversion rate, not the converted amount.

distractors.answer: The point where the line crosses the x-axis
distractors.explanation: The x-intercept is at zero, not at $40.

toLevel2.question: On a distance-time graph, what does a straight horizontal line mean?
toLevel2.correctExplanation: No change in distance over time means the object is stationary.

distractors.answer: The object is moving at constant speed
distractors.explanation: Constant speed shows a sloped line, not horizontal.
Acceleration shows a curving line, not horizontal.

toLevel2.question: A graph shows temperature over a day. The highest point on the curve represents the:
toLevel2.correct: Maximum temperature reached during the day
toLevel2.correctExplanation: The peak of a temperature-time curve is the day's maximum.

distractors.answer: Average temperature for the entire day
distractors.explanation: The average is not necessarily the highest point.

distractors.answer: Temperature at midnight on that day
distractors.explanation: Midnight is typically one of the coolest times.

toLevel2.question: What information can be found where two lines on a graph intersect?
toLevel2.correct: The values where both relationships are equal
toLevel2.correctExplanation: At an intersection, both lines share the same x-value and y-value.

distractors.answer: The rate of change of each line separately
distractors.explanation: Rates are found from gradients, not intersection points.

distractors.answer: The maximum value of both variables combined
distractors.explanation: An intersection does not indicate a maximum.

toLevel2.question: Which axis is the independent variable usually placed on?
toLevel2.correctExplanation: By convention, the independent variable goes on the x-axis (horizontal).

distractors.explanation: The vertical axis usually shows the dependent variable.
Each variable is assigned to one axis only.

toLevel2.question: A graph of plant height over weeks shows a straight line. What does the gradient tell?
toLevel2.correct: How many centimetres the plant grows per week
toLevel2.correctExplanation: The gradient is the rate of change: height gained per unit of time.

distractors.answer: The final height of the plant after all weeks
distractors.explanation: Final height is the last y-value, not the gradient.

distractors.answer: The number of weeks the plant was measured
distractors.explanation: That is the x-range, not the gradient.

toLevel2.question: On a graph, what does a line going downward from left to right indicate?
toLevel2.correct: The dependent variable decreases as x increases
toLevel2.correctExplanation: A downward slope means the y-value falls as the x-value rises.

distractors.answer: The dependent variable is increasing over time
distractors.explanation: Increasing would show an upward slope.

distractors.answer: There is no relationship between the variables
distractors.explanation: A clear downward trend shows a negative relationship.

toLevel2.sentence: On a distance-time graph, the {{blank:1}} axis shows time and the {{blank:2}} axis shows distance.

blanks.correctExplanation: Time is placed on the horizontal (x) axis by convention.

distractors.explanation: The vertical axis shows distance, not time.
Diagonal is not an axis name on a standard graph.

blanks.correctExplanation: Distance is placed on the vertical (y) axis by convention.

distractors.explanation: The horizontal axis shows time, not distance.
Diagonal is not a standard axis name.

toLevel2.sentence: A straight line on a graph indicates a {{blank:1}} relationship, while a curved line indicates a {{blank:2}} relationship.

blanks.correctExplanation: Linear means the rate of change is constant, producing a straight line.

distractors.explanation: Non-linear relationships produce curves, not straight lines.
A clear straight line shows a structured relationship, not randomness.

blanks.correctExplanation: Non-linear means the rate of change varies, producing a curve.

distractors.explanation: Linear relationships appear as straight lines, not curves.
Constant implies no change, which would be a horizontal line.

toLevel3.question: A steeper line on a conversion graph means a smaller conversion rate.
toLevel3.correctExplanation: A steeper line means a larger conversion rate; more of the second unit per one of the first.

distractors.explanation: A student choosing True reverses the meaning of gradient on a conversion graph.

toLevel3.question: If a distance-time graph is a straight line, the speed is constant.
toLevel3.correctExplanation: A straight line has a constant gradient, which represents constant speed.

distractors.explanation: A student choosing False may confuse straight lines with changing speed.

toLevel3.question: A graph showing temperature falling over time will have an upward-sloping line.
toLevel3.correctExplanation: Falling temperature means the y-value decreases, which produces a downward slope.

distractors.explanation: A student choosing True confuses the direction of temperature change with the slope direction.

toLevel3.question: The intersection of two lines on a graph shows where both quantities are equal.
toLevel3.correctExplanation: At the intersection point, both lines share the same coordinates.

distractors.explanation: A student choosing False may not realise that crossing lines share the same x and y values at that point.

toLevel3.question: A distance-time graph curving upward means the object is slowing down.
toLevel3.correctExplanation: Curving upward (getting steeper) means the speed is increasing, not decreasing.

distractors.explanation: A student choosing True confuses upward curvature with deceleration.

toLevel3.question: A horizontal line on a volume-time graph means no liquid is flowing.
toLevel3.correctExplanation: No change in volume over time indicates zero flow.

distractors.explanation: A student choosing False may think liquid can flow while the volume stays constant.

toLevel3.question: Two parallel lines on a graph must represent the same relationship.
toLevel3.correctExplanation: Parallel lines have the same gradient (rate) but different y-intercepts, so they represent different relationships with the same rate of change.

distractors.explanation: A student choosing True confuses same gradient with same relationship.

toLevel3.question: Reading values between plotted points on a graph is called extrapolation.
toLevel3.correctExplanation: Reading between known points is interpolation; extrapolation is reading beyond the data range.

distractors.explanation: A student choosing True confuses interpolation with extrapolation.

toLevel3.question: A distance-time graph shows a car covering 120 km in 2 hours at constant speed. What is the speed?
toLevel3.correctExplanation: Speed = distance divided by time = 120 divided by 2 = 60.

distractors.explanation: Multiplying distance by time gives 240, the wrong operation.
Adding 120 and 2 gives 122, an incorrect operation.

toLevel3.question: A conversion graph shows a straight line from the origin. What does this confirm?
toLevel3.correct: The conversion rate is constant throughout
toLevel3.correctExplanation: A straight line through the origin means y = mx, a constant rate.

distractors.answer: The values on the graph are unrelated
distractors.explanation: A clear line shows a strong relationship.

distractors.answer: The conversion rate changes at each point
distractors.explanation: A changing rate would produce a curve, not a straight line.

toLevel3.question: A graph shows water volume increasing steeply then becoming horizontal. What happened?
toLevel3.correct: Water filled quickly then the tap was turned off
toLevel3.correctExplanation: Steep rise means fast filling; horizontal means no further change.

distractors.answer: The tank started empty then was slowly drained
distractors.explanation: Draining would show a downward slope, not horizontal.

distractors.answer: Water flowed in faster toward the end of filling
distractors.explanation: Faster flow would make the line steeper, not horizontal.

toLevel3.question: On a distance-time graph, Mia's line is steeper than Tom's. What does this mean?
toLevel3.correctExplanation: Steeper gradient means more distance per unit time, which is greater speed.

distractors.answer: Tom ran further than Mia overall
distractors.explanation: Steepness indicates speed, not total distance.

distractors.answer: Mia started running later than Tom
distractors.explanation: Start time is shown by the x-intercept, not steepness.

toLevel3.question: A graph has a curved line that gets steeper over time. What type of relationship is this?
toLevel3.correct: Non-linear, because the rate of change increases
toLevel3.correctExplanation: A changing gradient means the relationship is not linear.

distractors.answer: Linear, because the graph line is increasing
distractors.explanation: Linear requires a constant rate; increasing does not mean linear.

distractors.answer: No relationship, because the line is not straight
distractors.explanation: A clear curve still shows a structured relationship.

toLevel3.question: A conversion graph passes through (0, 0) and (50, 40). What is the approximate y-value when x = 25?
toLevel3.correctExplanation: The line is straight through the origin, so at half of 50 the y-value is half of 40.

distractors.explanation: This reads the x-value as the y-value.
This underestimates by not using the proportional relationship.

toLevel3.question: A graph shows two lines meeting at (3, 12). What does the intersection mean in context?
toLevel3.correct: When x is 3, both relationships give y = 12
toLevel3.correctExplanation: At the intersection, both lines share coordinates (3, 12).

distractors.answer: Both variables equal 3 at that point
distractors.explanation: Only x equals 3; y equals 12 at the intersection.

distractors.answer: The lines have the same gradient at that point
distractors.explanation: Intersection means shared coordinates, not matching gradients.

toLevel3.question: A distance-time graph rises steeply then changes to a gentle slope. What happened to the speed?
toLevel3.correct: Speed decreased from fast to slow
toLevel3.correctExplanation: A steep line means high speed; a gentler slope means lower speed.

distractors.answer: Speed increased throughout the whole journey
distractors.explanation: Increasing speed would make the graph get steeper, not gentler.

distractors.answer: The object stopped then started again at speed
distractors.explanation: Stopping would show a horizontal section, not a gentle slope.

toLevel3.question: A Melbourne temperature graph shows 12 degrees at dawn, peaks at midday, then drops by evening. Is this linear?
toLevel3.correct: No, because the rate of change is not constant
toLevel3.correctExplanation: The temperature rises then falls, so the graph curves, not a straight line.

distractors.answer: Yes, because temperature changes over time
distractors.explanation: Change alone does not make a relationship linear.

distractors.answer: Yes, because there are three measured points
distractors.explanation: Three points can form a curve, not necessarily a line.

toLevel3.question: Which feature of a straight-line graph tells the rate of change?
toLevel3.correct: The gradient or slope of the line
toLevel3.correctExplanation: The gradient measures the change in y per unit change in x.

distractors.explanation: The y-intercept is the starting value, not the rate.
The x-intercept is where the line crosses the x-axis, not the rate.

toLevel3.question: Two runners' distance-time graphs cross at 4 minutes. Before that, Runner A is below Runner B. What does this mean?
toLevel3.correct: Runner B led until 4 minutes, then A overtook
toLevel3.correctExplanation: Below means less distance, so A was behind until the crossing point.

distractors.answer: Runner A was always ahead of Runner B
distractors.explanation: A was below B before the crossing, meaning A was behind.

distractors.answer: Runner B stopped running at the 4 minute mark
distractors.explanation: B stopping would show a horizontal line, not a crossing.

toLevel3.question: A graph shows fuel in a car decreasing over time. What does the steepness indicate?
toLevel3.correct: How quickly the fuel is being used
toLevel3.correctExplanation: A steeper downward slope means fuel is consumed at a faster rate.

distractors.answer: The total amount of fuel in the tank
distractors.explanation: Total fuel is the y-value, not the steepness.

distractors.answer: The total distance the car has travelled
distractors.explanation: Distance is not directly shown on a fuel-time graph.

toLevel3.sentence: On a distance-time graph, a steeper line indicates a {{blank:1}} speed, while a horizontal line means the object is {{blank:2}}.

blanks.correctExplanation: Steeper gradient = more distance per unit time = faster.

distractors.explanation: A gentler slope indicates slower speed, not a steeper one.
Any straight line shows constant speed; steepness determines how fast.

blanks.correctExplanation: Horizontal means zero change in distance over time.

distractors.explanation: Acceleration would show a curving line, not horizontal.
Deceleration would show a line becoming less steep, not horizontal.

toLevel3.sentence: The point where a graph line crosses the vertical axis is called the {{blank:1}}-intercept and shows the value when {{blank:2}} equals zero.

blanks.correctExplanation: The vertical axis is the y-axis, so the crossing is the y-intercept.

distractors.explanation: The x-intercept is where the line crosses the horizontal axis.
Standard two-dimensional graphs do not have a z-axis.

blanks.correctExplanation: At the y-intercept, the x-value is zero.

distractors.explanation: At the y-intercept, y has a specific value; x is zero.
Time may be the x-variable in some graphs but x is the general term.

toLevel3.sentence: A {{blank:1}} line on a graph represents a linear relationship, while a {{blank:2}} line represents a non-linear relationship.

blanks.correctExplanation: Linear relationships produce straight lines with constant gradient.

distractors.explanation: Curved lines show non-linear relationships.
Dotted is a line style, not a relationship type.

blanks.correctExplanation: Non-linear relationships have a changing rate, producing a curve.

distractors.explanation: Straight lines show linear relationships.
Horizontal is a type of straight line showing zero change.

toLevel3.sentence: When two lines on a graph {{blank:1}}, the variables share the same values at that point, called the {{blank:2}} point.

blanks.correctExplanation: Intersection is where two lines cross, sharing coordinates.

distractors.explanation: Separating means moving apart, not meeting.
Overlapping means the lines coincide entirely, not cross at a point.

blanks.correctExplanation: The shared point is called the intersection point.

distractors.explanation: A turning point is where a curve changes direction.
A maximum is the highest point on a curve, not where two lines cross.

toLevel3.sentence: On a conversion graph, the {{blank:1}} of the line tells the conversion rate, and a steeper line means a {{blank:2}} rate.

blanks.correctExplanation: The gradient (slope) represents how many units of one variable correspond to one unit of the other.

distractors.explanation: The length of a line segment does not indicate the conversion rate.
The y-intercept shows the starting value, not the rate.

blanks.correctExplanation: A steeper gradient means more output per unit of input.

distractors.explanation: A lower rate would produce a gentler slope, not a steeper one.
A zero rate would be a horizontal line, not steep.

toLevel3.sentence: Reading values between known data points on a graph is called {{blank:1}}, while reading beyond the data is called {{blank:2}}.

blanks.correctExplanation: Interpolation estimates values within the range of existing data.

distractors.explanation: Extrapolation goes beyond the data range.
Estimation is a general term; interpolation is the specific technique.

blanks.correctExplanation: Extrapolation extends the pattern beyond the known data.

distractors.explanation: Interpolation stays within the data range.
Prediction is broader; extrapolation is the graph-specific technique.

toLevel4.question: A car travels 180 km in 3 hours at constant speed, giving a gradient of 60 on its distance-time graph.
toLevel4.correctExplanation: Gradient = 180 divided by 3 = 60. This represents a speed of 60 km/h.

distractors.explanation: A student choosing False may miscalculate the gradient or confuse it with the total distance.

toLevel4.question: A graph showing a bath being filled then emptied would only have lines going upward.
toLevel4.correctExplanation: Filling produces an upward line; emptying produces a downward line.

distractors.explanation: A student choosing True forgets that emptying means volume decreases, requiring a downward slope.

toLevel4.question: A distance-time graph shows a straight line from (0, 0) to (4, 80). What is the speed?

distractors.explanation: Multiplying 80 by 4 gives 320, the wrong operation.
Subtracting 4 from 80 gives 76, an incorrect approach.

toLevel4.question: A conversion graph shows 1 AUD = 0.60 EUR. What is the euro value for 50 AUD?

distractors.explanation: Adding the rate to the amount instead of multiplying.
Dividing 50 by 0.60 gives approximately 83, the reverse conversion.

toLevel4.question: Cyclist A rides 12 km in 1 hour. Cyclist B rides 20 km in 2 hours. Which is faster?
toLevel4.correct: Cyclist A, with a speed of 12 km/h
toLevel4.correctExplanation: A: 12 km/h. B: 10 km/h. A is faster.

distractors.answer: Cyclist B, because 20 km is a further distance
distractors.explanation: Total distance does not determine speed; rate matters.

distractors.answer: Both travel at the same speed overall
distractors.explanation: 12 km/h and 10 km/h are different speeds.

toLevel4.question: A tank starts with 20 litres and fills at 5 litres per minute. What is the volume at 10 minutes?

distractors.explanation: Calculates 5 times 10 but forgets the starting 20 litres.
Multiplies 20 by 10, confusing the starting volume with a rate.

toLevel4.question: Lines y = 6x and y = 2x + 20 intersect at (5, 30). What does this intersection mean?
toLevel4.correct: At x = 5, both relationships give y = 30
toLevel4.correctExplanation: Both equations produce y = 30 when x = 5.

distractors.answer: Both lines have the same gradient throughout
distractors.explanation: The gradients are 6 and 2, which are different.

distractors.answer: The relationship y = 6x is always the larger value
distractors.explanation: Before x = 5, y = 2x + 20 is larger.

toLevel4.question: A temperature graph shows 15 degrees at 8 am and 25 degrees at 2 pm with a straight line. Estimate the temperature at 11 am.
toLevel4.correctExplanation: 11 am is halfway between 8 am and 2 pm. Midpoint: (15 + 25) divided by 2 = 20.

distractors.explanation: Overestimates by not finding the exact midpoint.
Underestimates by misjudging the time proportion.

toLevel4.question: A plant height graph passes through (0, 5) and (4, 25). What is the growth rate per week?
toLevel4.correctExplanation: Change in height: 25 minus 5 = 20. Divided by 4 weeks = 5 cm/week.

distractors.explanation: Uses the total height instead of the change.
Divides 25 by 4 without subtracting the starting height.

toLevel4.question: A fuel graph starts at 60 litres and drops to 20 litres over 4 hours. What is the consumption rate?
toLevel4.correctExplanation: Change: 60 minus 20 = 40. Divided by 4 hours = 10 litres/hour.

distractors.explanation: Divides 60 by 4 without subtracting the remaining fuel.
Divides 20 by 4, using the final amount instead of the change.

toLevel4.question: A distance-time graph goes from (0, 0) to (2, 30) then is horizontal to (5, 30). What happened at 2 hours?
toLevel4.correctExplanation: The horizontal section from (2, 30) to (5, 30) shows no distance change.

distractors.explanation: Increasing speed would make the line steeper, not horizontal.

distractors.answer: The object turned around and went back
distractors.explanation: Returning would show the line going downward, not horizontal.

toLevel4.question: A km-to-miles graph passes through (0, 0) and (8, 5). How many miles is 16 km?

distractors.explanation: Adds 8 and 5 instead of scaling proportionally.
Adds 16 and 5 instead of using the conversion rate.

toLevel4.question: Two tanks fill with water. Tank A has gradient 3, Tank B has gradient 5. Which fills faster?
toLevel4.correct: Tank B, because its gradient is steeper
toLevel4.correctExplanation: A gradient of 5 litres per minute is faster than 3.

distractors.answer: Tank A, because 3 comes before 5 numerically
distractors.explanation: Numerical order is irrelevant; a higher gradient means a faster rate.

distractors.answer: Both fill at the same rate over time
distractors.explanation: Different gradients mean different fill rates.

toLevel4.question: A line on a distance-time graph goes from (0, 10) to (3, 40). What is the speed?
toLevel4.correct: 10 km/h from change divided by time
toLevel4.correctExplanation: Change: 40 minus 10 = 30. Speed: 30 divided by 3 = 10 km/h.

distractors.answer: 13 km/h from total distance divided by time
distractors.explanation: Using 40 divided by 3 ignores the starting distance of 10.

distractors.answer: 30 km/h from distance change only without dividing
distractors.explanation: The change in distance must be divided by the change in time.

toLevel4.sentence: A car travels at constant speed. After 2 hours it has gone 100 km. The speed is 100 divided by {{blank:1}} = {{blank:2}} km/h.

blanks.correctExplanation: Time is 2 hours.

distractors.explanation: Dividing distance by itself gives 1, not the speed.
Using the answer as the divisor reverses the calculation.

blanks.correctExplanation: 100 divided by 2 = 50.

distractors.explanation: Multiplying instead of dividing gives 200.
Subtracting 2 from 100 gives 98, not the speed.

toLevel4.sentence: On a conversion graph, 10 AUD converts to 7 NZD. To convert 30 AUD, calculate 30 times {{blank:1}} divided by 10 = {{blank:2}} NZD.

blanks.correctExplanation: The conversion uses the ratio 7 NZD per 10 AUD.

distractors.explanation: Swaps the two currencies in the ratio.
Uses the amount to convert instead of the rate.

blanks.correctExplanation: 30 times 7 = 210, divided by 10 = 21.

distractors.explanation: Adds 30 and 7 instead of multiplying and dividing.
Multiplies 30 by 7 but forgets to divide by 10.

toLevel4.sentence: A tank starts with 10 litres and fills at 8 litres per minute. After 5 minutes, the volume is 10 + 8 times {{blank:1}} = {{blank:2}} litres.

blanks.correctExplanation: 5 minutes of filling at 8 litres per minute.

distractors.explanation: Swaps the rate and the time.
Confuses the initial volume with the time.
Calculates 8 times 5 = 40 but forgets the initial 10 litres.
Multiplies the rate by the initial volume instead.

toLevel4.sentence: Two lines y = 4x and y = 2x + 10 meet at the point ({{blank:1}}, {{blank:2}}).

blanks.correctExplanation: 4x = 2x + 10 gives 2x = 10, so x = 5.

distractors.explanation: Uses the constant from the second equation.
Uses the coefficient from the first equation.
Uses the constant from the second equation.
Adds both coefficients times 5: (4+2) times 5.

toLevel4.sentence: A fuel tank starts at 50 litres and empties at 8 litres per hour. After 5 hours, the fuel remaining is 50 minus {{blank:1}} = {{blank:2}} litres.

blanks.correctExplanation: 8 litres per hour times 5 hours = 40 litres used.

distractors.explanation: Uses the rate for one hour only.
Uses the number of hours instead of the total fuel used.
Subtracts only 8 (one hour) from 50.
Subtracts 5 (hours) from 50 instead of total fuel used.

toLevel4.sentence: A plant is 3 cm tall and grows 2 cm per week. After w weeks, height = 3 + {{blank:1}} times w. At 6 weeks, the height is {{blank:2}} cm.

blanks.correctExplanation: The growth rate is 2 cm per week.

distractors.explanation: Swaps the initial height with the growth rate.
Uses the number of weeks as the rate.
Calculates 2 times 6 but forgets the initial 3 cm.
Calculates 3 times 6, using the initial height as a rate.

toLevel4.sentence: A distance-time graph with constant speed from (0, 0) to (3, 90) has gradient {{blank:1}} divided by 3 = {{blank:2}} km/h.

blanks.correctExplanation: The change in distance is 90 km.

distractors.explanation: Uses the time value instead of the distance.
Uses the answer instead of the numerator.
